**ID:** Bu-Vb Np8  
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)  
**Collection:** Vinaya  
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 8  
**Title (English, from literature):** Requesting a fine robe from a fund  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin01m.mul4.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin01m.mul4.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Upakkhata Sutta* (Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 8) is a disciplinary text in the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka governing the acquisition of robes by Buddhist monks. The rule establishes that if a layperson has set aside a robe fund intended to purchase a robe for a monk, and that monk approaches the donor to request a particularly fine or expensive robe, he commits an offense requiring forfeiture of the robe (*nissaggiya*) and formal confession (*pācittiya*). An English translation of the rule and its accompanying analysis has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
